AZyfy4tocm.one_liner: Self-supervised 4D reconstruction trained from scratch on uncalibrated monocular video via latent cross-view reconstruction and constrained motion modeling
AZyfy4tocm.problem: Self-supervised learning has not yet been used to learn 3D structure and dynamics directly from raw video without camera calibration, geometric annotations or pretrained geometric models.
AZyfy4tocm.method: Scr4tch learns 4D representations that encode cross-view relationships through latent reconstruction, constrains motion modeling to separate camera motion from scene dynamics and suppress appearance shortcuts, and grounds them in an explicit deformable 4D scene by joint geometric optimization. It is trained on 2,154 hours of newly collected YouTube videos.
AZyfy4tocm.key_idea: Learn cross-view latent reconstruction while constraining motion modeling to separate camera motion from scene dynamics, then ground the representation in an explicit deformable 4D scene.
AZyfy4tocm.evidence: Experiments on unseen videos covering camera estimation, 4D reconstruction and novel view synthesis; datasets and baselines are not stated in the abstract.

jDSV8YrtWR.one_liner: GAE reparameterizes a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps.
jDSV8YrtWR.problem: Visual generators produce photorealistic frames without preserving scene geometry because their latents are organized around appearance while perception recovers geometry in a different space.
jDSV8YrtWR.method: The geometry-native autoencoder (GAE) makes a compact reparameterization of a geometry foundation model's feature space the generator's native latent, jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras and point maps, with a standard conditional flow on top.
jDSV8YrtWR.key_idea: Use a compact reparameterization of geometry foundation-model features as the generator's latent so one state decodes both appearance and 3D geometry.
jDSV8YrtWR.evidence: Controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, measuring visual quality (FVD) and independently measured 3D coherence.
jDSV8YrtWR.claimed_gains: Replacing the latent with GAE makes FVD fall by 12.7% and 23.1% on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K.

A6ElQ5Rm6E.one_liner: LADDER distills pretrained vision-language ViTs into hybrid attention-recurrent encoders that keep quality beyond the training resolution.
A6ElQ5Rm6E.problem: Linear recurrent CLIP encoders degrade sharply when sequence length moves beyond their low training resolution, while pretrained ViTs keep high-quality representations at larger resolutions.
A6ElQ5Rm6E.method: Converts pretrained vision-language ViTs into hybrid encoders that combine attention and recurrence within blocks (Vision-Delta recurrent patch mixing with an attention-based CLS) and across layers, placing full-attention layers under a fixed budget with reinforcement learning guided by cross-resolution teacher patch-feature recovery.
A6ElQ5Rm6E.key_idea: Reinforcement learning places a fixed budget of full-attention layers by cross-resolution teacher patch-feature recovery, and an attention-based CLS decouples global readout from recurrent blocks.
A6ElQ5Rm6E.evidence: Primary evaluation on TIPSv2 with additional validation on SigLIP2, after image-only training on ImageNet-1K.
A6ElQ5Rm6E.claimed_gains: With only 22 epochs of image-only training on ImageNet-1K, LADDER closely matches or surpasses its comparison models (the abstract is cut off before naming them).

VP9mj6YGw9.one_liner: Separates real motion from turbulence-induced pseudo-motion using phase-coherence cues inside a one-step diffusion model for infrared video super-resolution.
VP9mj6YGw9.problem: Turbulent infrared video super-resolution methods conflate turbulence-induced pseudo-motion with real object or camera motion, producing spurious alignments and unstable details.
VP9mj6YGw9.method: CAMO factorizes mixed temporal dynamics into constructive object motion and destructive turbulence components using a coherence reliability cue. The turbulence component suppresses local non-rigid distortions, the motion component promotes temporal consistency, and generative conditioning and velocity prediction are regulated by motion reliability.
VP9mj6YGw9.key_idea: Real motion induces coherent phase transport in infrared video while turbulence breaks that coherence, so coherence serves as the cue for splitting motion from turbulence.
VP9mj6YGw9.evidence: The visible abstract describes a physics-motivated design but does not state datasets or experimental settings.

Qn14WaPywU.one_liner: LOTUS steers frozen generative robot policies at inference by optimal-transport projection toward VLM-reward-induced action regions.
Qn14WaPywU.problem: Generative robot policies are brittle under train-test shifts, and retraining or fine-tuning is costly and may impair pretrained generalist capabilities.
Qn14WaPywU.method: LOTUS is training-free: a VLM synthesizes stage-wise reward functions, virtual trajectories are built along high-reward directions as samples of a task-aligned distribution, and the policy distribution is projected toward them as an OT problem with motion discrepancy as transport cost. The target marginal is relaxed to avoid over-steering toward implausible actions.
Qn14WaPywU.key_idea: Cast steering as optimal transport from the frozen policy's action distribution to reward-induced virtual trajectories, with a relaxed target marginal to keep the learned action prior.
Qn14WaPywU.evidence: Simulated and real-world manipulation tasks under diverse perturbations.
Qn14WaPywU.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports substantial improvement against diverse perturbations without numbers.

zUJXO6EKSo.one_liner: A single meta-learner aggregates delayed base learners to adapt to convex, strongly convex and exp-concave losses without curvature knowledge.
zUJXO6EKSo.problem: Online convex optimization with delayed feedback lacks one algorithm that adapts to general convex, strongly convex and exp-concave losses without prior knowledge of the curvature class or parameters.
zUJXO6EKSo.method: A delayed meta-learner with a second-order excess-loss guarantee aggregates delayed base learners in a curvature-adaptive way, together with a new exp-concave base learner.
zUJXO6EKSo.key_idea: Aggregate delayed base learners with a meta-learner having a second-order excess-loss guarantee, and bound exp-concave regret by the maximum number of simultaneously missing observations instead of the maximum delay.
zUJXO6EKSo.evidence: Regret bounds proved in the paper as stated in the abstract; no experiments are mentioned.
zUJXO6EKSo.claimed_gains: Regret of roughly sqrt(T + d_tot) for convex losses and sigma_max log T for curved losses, matching the best known dependence on T and delays up to doubly logarithmic factors.

z3s3MyZ0gz.one_liner: PAC-Bayes generalization bound for quantum policies whose complexity term is the log-determinant of the circuit's Fisher geometry, not parameter count.
z3s3MyZ0gz.problem: Parameterized quantum circuit policies in quantum RL are evaluated mostly by average return, leaving open when and why a quantum policy generalizes.
z3s3MyZ0gz.method: The paper gives a PAC-Bayesian bound for stochastic quantum policies whose complexity term is the log-determinant complexity of the circuit's Fisher geometry, set by entangling connectivity, readout locality and data re-uploading. A controlled setting fixes rotations, encoding and readout and varies only the entangling connectivity.
z3s3MyZ0gz.key_idea: Replace the parameter-count term in PAC-Bayes bounds with the log-determinant of the circuit's Fisher geometry, which circuit structure sets at a fixed parameter count.
z3s3MyZ0gz.evidence: A controlled experiment varying only entangling connectivity at fixed parameter count, comparing train-to-test gap against Fisher complexity and parameter count, plus unentangled circuits with data re-uploading and global readout.
z3s3MyZ0gz.claimed_gains: The train-to-test gap grows with Fisher complexity at fixed parameter count while parameter count is the weakest predictor, and the bound is a ranking certificate rather than a non-vacuous one.

Arz3pUTRwB.one_liner: Replaces dense BEV grids with 1D learnable map tokens built by joint self-attention with image tokens.
Arz3pUTRwB.problem: Online vectorized HD map construction usually relies on dense BEV grids, which need many tokens and memory, run slower, and depend on calibration metadata.
Arz3pUTRwB.method: A transformer mapper concatenates map and image tokens, applies full self-attention, discards the image tokens, and keeps the updated map tokens for decoding. The lightweight design lets the map decoder use full rather than deformable cross-attention.
Arz3pUTRwB.key_idea: Build a compact set of 1D map tokens by full self-attention over concatenated map and image tokens, then drop the image tokens.
Arz3pUTRwB.evidence: Experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 against dense BEV-based methods, including MapTRv2.
Arz3pUTRwB.claimed_gains: Uses up to 16.7x fewer intermediate tokens than dense BEV-based methods; the lightweight variant beats MapTRv2 by +10.1 mAP on nuScenes and +16.2 mAP on Argoverse 2.

tG1gE1D1Qq.one_liner: Bregman loss with an Aitchison-inspired potential, combining arithmetic-mean properness with sensitivity to relative label ratios in LDL.
tG1gE1D1Qq.problem: KL and squared Euclidean losses are mean-proper, but under limited model capacity or noisy data, small probability errors can distort relative label ratios near the simplex boundary.
tG1gE1D1Qq.method: Motivated by the squared Aitchison loss, which directly captures relative label ratios, the paper builds a Bregman loss with an Aitchison-inspired potential to reconcile mean-properness with ratio-sensitivity. The construction details are cut off in the abstract.
tG1gE1D1Qq.key_idea: Define the loss as a Bregman divergence whose potential is inspired by the squared Aitchison loss, aiming to reconcile arithmetic-mean properness with ratio-sensitivity.
tG1gE1D1Qq.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before any theory results or experiments are described.

345rqN2Lkw.one_liner: Tabular self-supervised learning that ranks true multi-column completions against product-of-marginals samples to learn conditional-to-marginal density ratios.
345rqN2Lkw.problem: Reconstruction and view-alignment objectives emphasize target prediction or instance-level invariance and may not capture the complex, multi-modal relationships among heterogeneous tabular features.
345rqN2Lkw.method: Conditional Completion Ranking (CCR) treats tabular SSL as learning the conditional-to-marginal shift of a multi-column candidate completion, and distinguishes samples from the joint distribution from samples drawn from the product of marginals.
345rqN2Lkw.key_idea: Train a discrimination objective between joint samples and product-of-marginals samples, whose optimal score recovers the log conditional-to-marginal density ratio.
345rqN2Lkw.evidence: Experiments on 50 datasets from two benchmarks under frozen and fine-tuned evaluation, plus a result that the optimal CCR score recovers the log density ratio.
345rqN2Lkw.claimed_gains: Best average rank in few-shot settings under both frozen and fine-tuned evaluation across 50 datasets from two benchmarks.

m2EFE8Uq8O.one_liner: Adds a learned per-token latent channel between denoising steps in masked diffusion models, trained with truncated BPTT.
m2EFE8Uq8O.problem: Masked diffusion models discard the internal computation over masked positions at each step, forcing every later refinement step to recompute it.
m2EFE8Uq8O.method: Relay introduces a differentiable per-token channel that passes information between forward passes, trained via 2-step truncated backpropagation through time. It is compatible with block diffusion and KV caching.
m2EFE8Uq8O.key_idea: Train a continuous cross-step relay end-to-end with truncated BPTT so the latent passed forward is optimized for the next denoising step.
m2EFE8Uq8O.evidence: Design choices justified on a Sudoku-based planning task, then scaled to Fast-dLLM v2 on coding tasks.
m2EFE8Uq8O.claimed_gains: Outperforms standard supervised finetuning on coding tasks while reducing inference latency by up to 32%.

FnECAZmjmq.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation for spoken dialogue models where a privileged-context teacher supervises a speech-only student, with chunk-level audio credit.
FnECAZmjmq.problem: Spoken dialogue models' semantic reasoning and paralinguistic responsiveness are limited by insufficient elicitation from speech alone, not by lack of capability.
FnECAZmjmq.method: VoxOPD has the student generate response trajectories from speech alone while a frozen teacher initialized from the same model, conditioned on privileged context, provides dense supervision along those trajectories. Beyond token-level distribution alignment, it assigns shared credit to audio segments through chunk-level supervision.
FnECAZmjmq.key_idea: Distill from a frozen same-model teacher given privileged context onto speech-only student rollouts, adding chunk-level supervision to handle local redundancy in discrete audio.
FnECAZmjmq.evidence: Step-Audio 2 mini evaluated on VoiceBench and VStyle, with further experiments on Kimi-Audio and other settings (abstract truncated).
FnECAZmjmq.claimed_gains: On Step-Audio 2 mini, improves the VoiceBench capability-specific task average by 4.0 and VStyle by 0.71.

ruNZQYtXsp.one_liner: Transports OOD non-member membership-inference scores to the target distribution and corrects audit inflation using calibration tasks.
ruNZQYtXsp.problem: In observational privacy auditing, where the auditor cannot insert canaries or retrain, the available non-members may be out-of-distribution, which skews membership-inference scores and the resulting audit.
ruNZQYtXsp.method: Learns the relationship between data representations and membership-inference scores from OOD non-members and transports it to the target covariate distribution to estimate the counterfactual in-distribution non-member score distribution. Adds a conservative correction calibrated to the nominal transported privacy level, using controlled calibration tasks built from the available non-member data to estimate how representation-space displacement inflates the audit.
ruNZQYtXsp.key_idea: Learn a representation-to-score map on OOD non-members, transport it to the target covariates, and correct for representation-space displacement using calibration-task estimates of audit inflation.
ruNZQYtXsp.evidence: Calibration tasks are built from the available non-member data to estimate audit inflation, but datasets, models and results are not stated in the visible abstract.

KQLAemmixL.one_liner: Classifies when spectrum-dependent adaptive normalizers, such as Newton-Schulz iterations, define one fixed convex geometry.
KQLAemmixL.problem: Finite spectral updates can approximate the polar direction without implementing any one fixed convex geometry, and it is unclear which adaptive normalizers do implement one.
KQLAemmixL.method: Analyzes filters q_i(s)=h(s_i/alpha(s)) whose scale depends on the spectrum, proving when a norm-derived direction or a positive C^1 integrating factor exists, and classifies adaptive normalizers whose response lies in one fixed convex subdifferential. Also gives a perspective construction with one norm per depth whose gradient approximates the Taylor fields uniformly as depth grows.
KQLAemmixL.key_idea: Test whether a spectrum-dependent normalized filter admits a norm-derived direction (a positive integrating factor), which holds exactly when h(t)=at+ct^(2k+1) and fails for repeated cubic Newton-Schulz steps.
KQLAemmixL.evidence: Proofs under stated regularity assumptions in dimensions two to four and above, plus replay of 4,728 unique stored spectra to quantify finite-depth approximation and paired small-decoder experiments (abstract truncated).

DmqCKGPSvS.one_liner: 3D point tracker that de-duplicates co-located tracks by voxelization at sliding-window boundaries to track all points over 1000+ frames.
DmqCKGPSvS.problem: Existing point trackers either follow a sparse set of query points over long horizons or track all points only over short clips.
DmqCKGPSvS.method: Represents video as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates and merges co-located tracks at sliding-window boundaries through voxelization. Splits tracking into an endpoint refiner that predicts each point's destination and static-versus-dynamic class, followed by a lightweight trajectory refiner that decodes dense trajectories only for dynamic points.
DmqCKGPSvS.key_idea: Voxelization-based de-duplication of co-located tracks at window boundaries ties model complexity to unique scene geometry rather than to video length.
DmqCKGPSvS.evidence: Evaluated on TAPVid-3D against open-source all-frame dense 3D trackers and sparse trackers on short clips, with a long-video claim for 1000+ frames within 40 GB of GPU memory (abstract truncated).
DmqCKGPSvS.claimed_gains: Outperforms open-source all-frame dense 3D trackers by more than 20% APD on short clips on TAPVid-3D, and tracks all visible points in videos exceeding 1000 frames within 40 GB of GPU memory.

R9cPF2SmWS.one_liner: Benchmark of 492 tasks over 77 native Linux TUI tools for agents acting by keyboard on a character viewport.
R9cPF2SmWS.problem: Terminal agent evaluation assumes a shell-command interface, leaving full-screen native text user interfaces such as editors, file managers and debuggers unmeasured.
R9cPF2SmWS.method: TUI-Bench has 492 tasks across 77 native Linux TUI tools in 19 application categories; each task starts inside the running program, exposes a plain-text 32 x 96 viewport with cursor coordinates, permits only keyboard actions, and is scored by deterministic verifiers of application state, preserved data and whether the program should still be running.
R9cPF2SmWS.key_idea: Score agents on keyboard-only control of running full-screen TUIs with deterministic state verifiers on a 32 x 96 plain-text viewport.
R9cPF2SmWS.evidence: A three-round evaluation of frontier models on the 492 tasks, reporting that the strongest models solve only a small fraction of scored episodes.

O3x53JdSlh.one_liner: Contextual bandit with cascade browsing and multinomial-logit choice, solved by a modified planning step and a UCB algorithm.
O3x53JdSlh.problem: In recommender systems users browse only a prefix of a displayed list before choosing, so item selection and order both matter, and finding the optimal sequence is a hard combinatorial planning problem even with known parameters.
O3x53JdSlh.method: Introduces contextual cascade browsing bandits (CCBB), which model sequential browsing and terminal choice with a multinomial logit model, modifies the sequencing step of an existing planning procedure to get a stronger worst-case approximation guarantee, and proposes CCBB-UCB, which combines that planner with optimistic exploration.
O3x53JdSlh.key_idea: Use the structure of the approximate planning problem to establish optimism of the sequence-level reward estimate, even though item-level optimistic estimates do not guarantee it.
O3x53JdSlh.evidence: Regret analysis of CCBB-UCB and a structural analysis of the planned sequence; experiments are not stated in the visible abstract.
O3x53JdSlh.claimed_gains: CCBB-UCB achieves O~(d sqrt(T)) approximation-scaled regret, with a stronger worst-case approximation guarantee for planning (no ratio stated).

TAlvj5yuBH.one_liner: Shows multi-view clustering and ensemble clustering are equivalent via a latent co-association matrix shared across delta-sensitive co-association matrices.
TAlvj5yuBH.problem: Directly casting ensemble clustering as a multi-view clustering problem is hard, and existing ensemble methods either linearly combine connective matrices or refine the co-association matrix with a coherent-link matrix.
TAlvj5yuBH.method: Builds multiple co-association matrices through a delta-sensitive feature descriptor and introduces one latent co-association matrix shared across them, so the equivalence follows from the objective formulation. Defines a delta-sensitive margin and proves that the descriptor yields the largest such margin.
TAlvj5yuBH.key_idea: Define delta-sensitive feature descriptors that yield several co-association matrices, and tie them to one shared latent co-association matrix in a multi-view clustering objective.
TAlvj5yuBH.evidence: A proof that the delta-sensitive descriptor generates the largest delta-sensitive margin; experiments are not visible in the truncated abstract.

IfND4Uw8qO.one_liner: Autoregressive SumComposer adds video segments conditioned on prior selections, trained on pseudo-summaries built offline from frame-importance labels.
IfND4Uw8qO.problem: Video summarization work predicts frame importance but leaves segmentation and budget-constrained selection as a fixed pipeline, and more precise importance scores do not reliably produce better summaries.
IfND4Uw8qO.method: Offline pseudo-summary construction turns existing frame-importance annotations and video content into structured, budget-aware pseudo-summaries. SumComposer then autoregressively adds a segment to the summary conditioned on preceding selections, and needs neither importance annotations nor language model calls at inference.
IfND4Uw8qO.key_idea: Train summary composition directly by autoregressive segment selection on budget-aware pseudo-summaries derived from frame-importance annotations.
IfND4Uw8qO.evidence: Experiments show the pseudo-summaries align better with human annotations than fixed construction, and SumComposer trained on them improves matching and boundary alignment over fixed composition.

o2fVnEP3rN.one_liner: Characterizes regularizers needing no subsequent-action sampling and derives a variance-minimizing implicit-reward correction for convex regularizers in off-policy preference optimization.
o2fVnEP3rN.problem: Convex regularizers other than reverse KL perform worse in preference optimization, especially off-policy, because in multi-step MDPs estimating the implicit reward requires sampling subsequent actions from the current policy, which compounds estimation errors.
o2fVnEP3rN.method: They formally characterize regularizers that need no subsequent action sampling and prove reverse KL is unique in giving a closed-form solution. For other convex regularizers, they propose a regularity condition that minimizes the variance of the implicit reward estimator and derive a canonical form satisfying it by design.
o2fVnEP3rN.key_idea: Choose the implicit-reward estimator for separable convex regularizers that minimizes estimator variance through a regularity condition, so errors do not compound along trajectories.
o2fVnEP3rN.evidence: Tabular MDPs and large language model post-training, compared with alternative approaches for estimating separable convex regularizers, plus a formal characterization and uniqueness proof.
o2fVnEP3rN.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says the correction consistently improves on alternative approaches to estimating separable convex regularizers, without numbers.

enCg96m4Dp.one_liner: MOON adds a deviation judge that clears visual history and a GRPO-trained recovery policy to a frozen VLN policy
enCg96m4Dp.problem: Vision-and-language navigation policies that act on visual history can be taken off route by a wrong action, and after a deviation the retained history keeps the policy from turning where needed (behavioral inertia).
enCg96m4Dp.method: Equips a frozen VLN policy with two lightweight modules adding less than 1% of its parameters: a deviation judge that raises an alarm clearing the history when it predicts the agent is off route, and a recovery policy trained with GRPO from alarm states.
enCg96m4Dp.key_idea: Clear visual history only when a judge detects deviation, and train a GRPO recovery policy from alarm states so successes found by sampling appear in greedy rollouts.
enCg96m4Dp.evidence: Paired interventions on four VLN policies, experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE with a random-trigger ablation, zero-shot object-goal navigation on HM3D-OVON, and a real robot.
enCg96m4Dp.claimed_gains: Clearing history doubles pooled success at the onset of a deviation; MOON reaches the highest R2R-CE success rate among compared methods and raises the success rate of its frozen base by 5.2 and 6.0 points, with less than 1% additional parameters.

1OW8KrZY8s.one_liner: Lightweight 33M cross-encoder reranks videos from cached compact frame tokens, avoiding query-time visual encoding.
1OW8KrZY8s.problem: Joint video-text matching improves retrieval, but processing rich video representations for each query is costly.
1OW8KrZY8s.method: VEDJE compresses features within sampled frames while keeping their representations separate in a reusable cache. Feature-change prediction supplies an auxiliary training signal that improves retrieval from the compressed cache without adding query-time work.
1OW8KrZY8s.key_idea: Cache per-frame compressed tokens offline and train a cross-encoder reranker on them with an auxiliary feature-change prediction loss.
1OW8KrZY8s.evidence: MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and ActivityNet against matched first-stage retrievers in both retrieval directions, including fine-tuned VideoCLIP-XL and VideoPrism configurations; the TL;DR also states the 33M cross-encoder matches 7B MLLM rerankers.
1OW8KrZY8s.claimed_gains: Reaches 59.8 text-to-video R@1 on MSR-VTT with a fine-tuned VideoCLIP-XL first stage, and shrinking the per-video cache fourfold to 12 KiB preserves text-to-video recall within 0.2 points in the VideoPrism configuration.

LSxjUXtNNe.one_liner: Training-free merge of seed-wise fine-tuned LLMs by aligning low-rank SVD subspaces and combining orientations (Procrustes) and scales separately.
LSxjUXtNNe.problem: Fine-tuning large language models has high variance across random seeds, forcing repeated runs or expensive ensembles to reach top performance.
LSxjUXtNNe.method: Per layer, SWIN computes low-rank SVDs, forms basis-invariant projection operators for a shared left/right consensus subspace, and decouples each seed's core update into orientation and scale by polar decomposition. It aggregates orientations with a Procrustes projection, averages symmetric scales, and reconstructs a single low-rank update.
LSxjUXtNNe.key_idea: Merge seed updates in a shared SVD subspace by combining orientation (Procrustes) and scale separately, instead of element-wise weight averaging.
LSxjUXtNNe.evidence: Mathematical reasoning, commonsense reasoning, code generation, and RL benchmarks, compared with the best individual seed and element-wise merging baselines.
LSxjUXtNNe.claimed_gains: Consistently matches or exceeds the best individual seed and improves MetaMath and AIME by up to +4.0 and +9.9 absolute points over element-wise baselines, with no extra training or inference overhead.

ha1E1bva10.one_liner: ROMA is an LLM system that actively chooses interactions and sensors to gather multi-sensory evidence about real objects.
ha1E1bva10.problem: Existing multi-sensory robot systems integrate sensory inputs but do not actively acquire missing evidence through interaction.
ha1E1bva10.method: ROMA runs a reasoning-interaction-feedback loop over vision, audio, tactile, and force sensing; ROMA-7B is fine-tuned in two stages on the ROMI-2K dataset to assess evidence sufficiency and select interactions.
ha1E1bva10.key_idea: Let an LLM decide what evidence is missing, which object, interaction, and modality to use next, then reason over the executed interaction's multi-sensory feedback.
ha1E1bva10.evidence: ROMI-2K, a real-world dataset of nearly 2,000 object-content combinations and 6 atomic interactions with synchronized feedback; the rest of the abstract is cut off.

Pezz4qs7vo.one_liner: DUET regulates cross-modal hashing under noisy labels using temporal and instantaneous consensus signals to weight modality contributions.
Pezz4qs7vo.problem: Under noisy labels, modalities respond differently to the same supervision, so uniform cross-modal semantic alignment can propagate unstable predictions.
Pezz4qs7vo.method: Temporal Consensus Learning aggregates predictions across epochs to measure stability, and Modality Consensus Learning uses the concentration of current prediction distributions to set each modality's contribution and consensus constraint.
Pezz4qs7vo.key_idea: Condition cross-modal semantic interaction on two reliability cues, epoch-wise prediction stability and per-modality prediction concentration, instead of aligning all modalities equally.
Pezz4qs7vo.evidence: Experiments on three benchmark datasets; the abstract is cut off before details.

fZfLzRSJhY.one_liner: Agent co-develops RTL and an executable Behavior IR model, enabling latency-tolerant verification and RL training for hardware design.
fZfLzRSJhY.problem: Cycle-by-cycle output matching rejects valid hardware designs whose latency differs, so agents lack reliable feedback on functional correctness.
fZfLzRSJhY.method: BEHAVE defines Behavior IR, executable behavior models in restricted Python, and has the agent iteratively develop an RTL design and its own behavior model, comparing inputs and outputs across task-permitted latencies and using EDA tool feedback for PPA trade-offs. BEHAVE-Sim checks both artifacts against a hidden golden behavior model with solver-guided test generation, and its scores serve as RL rewards for multi-turn training.
fZfLzRSJhY.key_idea: Use a restricted-Python functional behavior model as a timing-agnostic reference, so designs are verified by logical input-output comparison rather than cycle-exact matching.
fZfLzRSJhY.evidence: Evaluation through BEHAVE-Sim against hidden golden behavior models and RL training on specification-behavior pairs; datasets and results are cut off in the visible abstract.

1do7M8Z7r2.one_liner: Ladder Transformer is an encoder-decoder trained with input-space losses only on a single token stream of continuous multimodal data.
1do7M8Z7r2.problem: The abstract gives no explicit gap; it targets one model for representation learning and generation across continuous and discrete modalities with heterogeneous sampling rates.
1do7M8Z7r2.method: Modalities such as text, video, audio and proprioception are treated as one token stream, with native support for heterogeneous sampling rates. Training uses only input-space losses, with no EMA teacher, auxiliary losses or anti-collapse regulariser.
1do7M8Z7r2.key_idea: Treat all modalities as a single token stream in an encoder-decoder trained purely by input-space reconstruction, without teacher or anti-collapse machinery.
1do7M8Z7r2.evidence: Frozen-feature video classification compared with existing masked modelling methods, plus a variety of autoregressive generation tasks.
1do7M8Z7r2.claimed_gains: Stronger temporal understanding than existing masked modelling methods on frozen-feature video classification; no numbers stated.

0dyabevIEO.one_liner: Zero-shot sequential recommender, trained only on synthetic data, that adapts in context through ID-based pointer attention over support sequences.
0dyabevIEO.problem: Sequential recommendation in new domains typically requires extensive per-dataset training data and compute.
0dyabevIEO.method: ICR is a Prior-Fitted Network that takes support sequences from the target and produces next-item predictions in one forward pass, using a synthetic prior with full support over finite item sequences, an ID-based architecture with a pointer mechanism selecting items from context, and identity-restricted cross-attention.
0dyabevIEO.key_idea: Pretrain on a synthetic prior built from a hierarchy of aggregation functions and select items by pointer over context IDs, so predictions rely on in-context sequences rather than absolute embeddings.
0dyabevIEO.evidence: 11 benchmark datasets against zero-shot and supervised baselines, plus theory on prior support and independence from absolute embedding coordinates.
0dyabevIEO.claimed_gains: On the majority of 11 benchmark datasets, ICR outperforms every zero-shot baseline and matches or exceeds standard supervised baselines.

7J2DXTCEwz.one_liner: Fine-tunes LLMs on matched Safe-Unsafe instruction pairs with boundary annotations, adding a contrastive regularizer for safety-relevant representation shifts.
7J2DXTCEwz.problem: Imprecise safe/unsafe boundaries in LLMs cause both unsafe compliance and over-refusal of safe but sensitive requests.
7J2DXTCEwz.method: Builds semantically matched Safe-Unsafe pairs annotated with the preserved non-safety semantic frame, the safety-critical factor, and the required policy behavior, then applies Boundary-Constrained Fine-Tuning (SFT plus Safety Contrastive Regularization). At deployment the model generates a bounded structured annotation before its visible answer.
7J2DXTCEwz.key_idea: Train on counterfactual pairs that flip only the safety-critical factor, with a contrastive regularizer that shifts safety-relevant representations while preserving shared non-safety utility.
7J2DXTCEwz.evidence: A revised eight-condition HarmBench evaluation on Qwen2.5-7B, with XSTest over-refusal and MT-Bench utility.
7J2DXTCEwz.claimed_gains: Reduces HarmBench attack success from 58.4% to 6.6% on Qwen2.5-7B, with 2.1% XSTest over-refusal and an MT-Bench score of 7.84.

MxaVFeHwPw.one_liner: Shows diffusion language models keep old decisions after answer reopening via retained rationale, unless both rationale and answer are reopened.
MxaVFeHwPw.problem: Diffusion language models appear revisable because tokens are generated at many positions, but previously generated rationale can reconstruct the old decision even when new evidence is available.
MxaVFeHwPw.method: Compares reopening the answer alone with reopening both rationale and answer, and exchanges rationales between paired trajectories (rationale transplantation); token-level attribution is tested for choosing which positions to reopen.
MxaVFeHwPw.key_idea: Corrigibility depends on retained rationale state: reopening only the answer lets old rationale rebuild the prior decision, while reopening both lets decisions follow current evidence.
MxaVFeHwPw.evidence: A 150-question source-disjoint benchmark on Dream, LLaDA, and iLLaDA, and a new 100-question free-form short-answer evaluation.

wuOaZqBgkd.one_liner: Applies Follow-the-Regularized-Leader to robust Markov games and proves matching upper and lower sample-complexity bounds for robust CCE.
wuOaZqBgkd.problem: Sample complexity for robust Markov games suffers from the curse of multiple agents, and prior FTRL-based results have worse dependence on horizon H and accuracy epsilon than earlier work.
wuOaZqBgkd.method: In the finite-horizon setting with an R-contamination uncertainty set and a generative model, they apply FTRL to find an epsilon-robust coarse correlated equilibrium. They also establish an information-theoretic lower bound under the same uncertainty model.
wuOaZqBgkd.key_idea: FTRL run on the finite-horizon R-contamination robust Markov game with a generative model, giving sample complexity that scales with the sum of agents' action counts rather than their product.
wuOaZqBgkd.evidence: Theory only as stated: an upper bound for FTRL and a matching information-theoretic lower bound under the R-contamination model; no empirical experiments are stated.
wuOaZqBgkd.claimed_gains: Sample complexity (up to log factors) of O~(H^3 S sum_{i=1}^m A_i min{H,1/R} / eps^2) for an eps-robust CCE, with a matching lower bound.

FozQwLlee0.one_liner: Learns dynamic manipulation from one static demonstration via synthesized dynamic demos and an inference-frequency-adaptive imitation policy.
FozQwLlee0.problem: Dynamic manipulation needs large data because of combinatorial scenario complexity, and rapid dynamics require real-time, accurate policy execution.
FozQwLlee0.method: A static-to-dynamic augmentation pipeline synthesizes diverse dynamic demonstrations from a single static demonstration, and a dynamic-aware adaptive policy adjusts its inference frequency to task dynamics. They also build a dynamic manipulation benchmark with an automatic evaluation system.
FozQwLlee0.key_idea: Synthesize dynamic demonstrations from one static demo by augmentation, and let the policy vary its inference frequency according to how fast the task dynamics change.
FozQwLlee0.evidence: Experiments in simulation and the real world, including a newly built dynamic manipulation benchmark.
FozQwLlee0.claimed_gains: Mean success rate 18.4 percentage points higher; the policy-query latency improvement figure is cut off in the abstract.

bXd1UOqOzO.one_liner: Decomposes team loss at a handoff into the agent's error, the partner's missing information and its misused information.
bXd1UOqOzO.problem: A strong agent sharing control with a weaker partner can leave states the partner cannot handle even when each of its own actions is sound, and behavior alone cannot separate the sources of loss.
bXd1UOqOzO.method: They define handoff regret and show team loss relative to the solo optimum equals the agent's own error plus the handed-over loss under the partner's rule, which splits into the value of information the partner lacks and its decision error. The same accounting yields partner-aware corrections to an existing value oracle with explicit error terms.
bXd1UOqOzO.key_idea: Split handed-over loss exactly into the value of the partner's missing information (a Blackwell-style refinement order) and its decision error, then correct a value oracle with partner-aware terms.
bXd1UOqOzO.evidence: Theory (exact decomposition, refinement order, a construction with unbounded gain per unit of solo loss), tag-team chess with Maia-2 partners under strict alternation, and navigation interventions.
bXd1UOqOzO.claimed_gains: In tag-team chess the partner-aware correction beats an engine with the same search budget head to head at 57.2% of points, while the extra search alone gains nothing.

FNCYKCHUlz.one_liner: Benchmark of 260 test cases measuring static and dynamic memory in video world models through camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories.
FNCYKCHUlz.problem: As video world models produce longer interactive experiences, there is no systematic evaluation of whether they keep the world consistent with its history.
FNCYKCHUlz.method: WorldMemBench assesses static memory (human identity and appearance, object appearance and geometry, environment content and geometry) and dynamic memory (event progression, state persistence) using controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories, combining appearance and geometry metrics with event-specific assessments.
FNCYKCHUlz.key_idea: Test memory by leaving and revisiting scene content along controlled camera paths and scoring against fixed references and expected state transitions.
FNCYKCHUlz.evidence: Nine representative video world models evaluated on 260 test cases, with human studies checking alignment between automatic and human judgments.
FNCYKCHUlz.claimed_gains: not stated; reported findings are that static retention does not imply reliable dynamic state evolution and that memory degrades with repeated revisits.

OpUTpvmgQl.one_liner: Steers attention in multi-agent LLM systems toward relevant context using the structure of agent communication.
OpUTpvmgQl.problem: Long multi-agent communication histories dilute relevant information, and compress-or-prune methods may discard subtle but critical details.
OpUTpvmgQl.method: Agent-Radar is an attention steering method that uses the inherent structure of multi-agent communication to dynamically guide each agent's attention toward relevant context at every reasoning step while keeping the full history.
OpUTpvmgQl.key_idea: Steer attention toward relevant earlier messages using the communication structure between agents, recomputed as the conversation evolves, instead of compressing history.
OpUTpvmgQl.evidence: Five benchmarks, with analyses varying the number of agents and interaction rounds and ablations of core components.
OpUTpvmgQl.claimed_gains: Average gain of 4.17 absolute points over the strongest baseline across five benchmarks.

8dA1IhEZaU.one_liner: Generates image-retouching tool parameters from noise with conditional rectified flow instead of autoregressive MLLM tool calls.
8dA1IhEZaU.problem: Tool-based image editing with autoregressive MLLMs sequentially generates reasoning, tool selections and parameter values, which the paper shows is slow and memory-heavy compared with direct generation.
8dA1IhEZaU.method: FlowTool models the distribution of high-quality tool parameters given the image and instruction with conditional rectified flow: a vision-language backbone feeds a Diffusion Transformer parameter generator that turns Gaussian noise into an editing plan. Training uses a two-stage supervised flow-matching curriculum, then reward-based post-training.
8dA1IhEZaU.key_idea: Treat the editing plan as a structured parameter vector sampled by conditional rectified flow from Gaussian noise, replacing sequential token generation.
8dA1IhEZaU.evidence: MMArt-Bench, FlowTool-Eval, ArtEdit-Bench and MIT-Adobe5K, against specialized MLLM editing agents and proprietary MLLMs.
8dA1IhEZaU.claimed_gains: Reduces latency by at least 50x and needs nearly 2x less memory than the compared baselines, with stronger reference-based performance than specialized MLLM editing agents and proprietary MLLMs.

Yo57XNCOA2.one_liner: A 299K-parameter frozen adapter that refines and upsamples vision foundation model features for aerial visible-infrared perception.
Yo57XNCOA2.problem: Vision foundation models are pretrained mostly on RGB and not optimized for cross-spectral visible-infrared cues, while dedicated VI pretraining needs costly registered pairs and existing VI adapters are tied to specific encoders and tasks.
Yo57XNCOA2.method: AnyVIA is pretrained once and reused frozen across VFMs and tasks. For each modality a Raw Guidance Encoder derives attention queries and keys only from the input image while host features enter as values; pretraining uses shared box prompts and a directional consistency objective aligning refined features with frozen host features from higher-resolution crops, on the constructed UAVRGBT235K dataset.
Yo57XNCOA2.key_idea: Compute attention queries and keys from the raw image only and feed host features solely as values, decoupling adapter weights from the host encoder.
Yo57XNCOA2.evidence: Pretraining on the constructed UAVRGBT235K dataset and reuse across heterogeneous VFMs and downstream tasks; the abstract is truncated before results.
Yo57XNCOA2.claimed_gains: not stated; only the 299K adapter size is given.

HDzRXC2Iu5.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether agent memory systems infer user habits from weak longitudinal evidence and apply them to later requests.
HDzRXC2Iu5.problem: Individual observations give only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies, and retaining past interactions alone does not ensure agents infer and apply habits appropriately.
HDzRXC2Iu5.method: HABIT-Bench builds synthetic user histories of hundreds of sessions from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks cover temporary exceptions, habit changes, and unaccepted suggestions, with independent human review of sampled tasks.
HDzRXC2Iu5.key_idea: Generate user histories from controlled habit graphs so memory systems must induce habits from partial evidence, including exceptions and changes.
HDzRXC2Iu5.evidence: Eight memory methods evaluated with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash.
HDzRXC2Iu5.claimed_gains: The best memory method reaches 33.61% macro accuracy across the four domains, and performance stays limited even when annotated evidence is supplied directly.

YMcnBtdhGJ.one_liner: Trains generative process reward models with outcome-only RL, rewarding only the final outcome label after step-level CoT checks.
YMcnBtdhGJ.problem: Training strong PRMs is costly: human step annotation does not scale, and Monte Carlo estimates are expensive and can drift from intrinsic step correctness.
YMcnBtdhGJ.method: TIPS has the model generate a chain-of-thought followed by step-level labels and an outcome label; the reward depends only on whether the outcome matches ground truth, and the group-relative advantage optimizes the whole response, so more accurate step checks that improve outcome judgments are reinforced.
YMcnBtdhGJ.key_idea: Reward only the final outcome label so group-relative RL indirectly reinforces accurate step-level verification inside the chain-of-thought.
YMcnBtdhGJ.evidence: Math and agent benchmarks across four backbone families, including ProcessBench with TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507.
YMcnBtdhGJ.claimed_gains: TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 reaches 85.2 F1 on ProcessBench with only 3.2K outcome-labeled trajectories, surpassing all evaluated trained PRMs and prompt-only judges such as GPT-5.4-Instruct and Claude-4.7-Opus.

GEavK4L76f.one_liner: Agentic 3D composition framework where an Assembly Agent and a Critic Agent iterate using physical simulation.
GEavK4L76f.problem: Prior LLM coordinate prediction and diffusion-prior image synthesis rely on static priors and struggle with precise hanging, gravity-driven settling, and hidden containment, which need interactive construction with planning, fine alignment, and physics.
GEavK4L76f.method: PhySGA uses a feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent does geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, and a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics (the rest is truncated) with physical simulation. It targets rigid, articulated, and deformable objects.
GEavK4L76f.key_idea: Ground agent planning in physical simulation through an assembly agent and a critic agent that reasons over contact dynamics.
GEavK4L76f.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; datasets and baselines are not visible.

7AQhDIxKW1.one_liner: Regime-aware off-policy RL family using sample weight decay and per-regime stabilizer choices for massively parallel simulation.
7AQhDIxKW1.problem: Canonical off-policy stabilizers were designed for data-limited training with narrow replay coverage, and their roles are unclear when massively parallel simulation supplies abundant diverse data.
7AQhDIxKW1.method: After a controlled study across eight benchmark families, WarpSAC applies Sample Weight Decay as a regime-agnostic component and matches each data regime with a prescribed variant, such as WarpSAC-L (Norm ON, clipped double-Q); the remaining variants are cut off in the abstract.
7AQhDIxKW1.key_idea: Select stabilizers (parameter normalization, clipped double-Q) per data regime and add Sample Weight Decay as a regime-agnostic exploitation component.
7AQhDIxKW1.evidence: Controlled empirical study across eight benchmark families spanning CPU-scale locomotion, GPU-parallel robotic simulation, dexterous manipulation, and humanoid whole-body control.

P7JCS0QuoN.one_liner: Replaces natural-language reasoning before image generation with a structured scene-object-relation language, trained by SFT and structure-reward GRPO.
P7JCS0QuoN.problem: Unified multimodal models added explicit natural-language reasoning before image generation by default, and this paper questions whether that is the right reasoning representation.
P7JCS0QuoN.method: The UMM generates VSRL (global scene, objects, and their relations) from a prompt and conditions image generation on it. A pipeline builds verified prompt-VSRL-image triplets for supervised fine-tuning, and StruFlow-GRPO jointly optimizes reasoning and generation with programmatic structure rewards and image rewards.
P7JCS0QuoN.key_idea: Reason in a structured language of global scene, objects, and relations rather than free text, and reward structure programmatically.
P7JCS0QuoN.evidence: On BAGEL across six generation benchmarks against the base model and native Self CoT; on Cheers, separately trained VSRL and natural-language CoT models evaluated on GenEval and TIIF-Bench.
P7JCS0QuoN.claimed_gains: Compared with Self CoT, GenEval Short improves from 79.0 to 88.9 and OneIG-Bench from 32.4 to 43.7.

RVwzfd0hd6.one_liner: Predicts the current latent image features from the stale RGB frame and intervening events using frozen-teacher cross-time distillation.
RVwzfd0hd6.problem: Asynchronous RGB-event detectors fuse current events with stale features from the previous RGB frame, and this temporal mismatch limits detection accuracy between RGB arrivals.
RVwzfd0hd6.method: PRED predicts the current latent image representation from the previous RGB frame and subsequent events before fusion. A teacher is first trained with access to the current RGB frame and then frozen to supply stable latent targets (two-stage cross-time distillation); the HiFE dataset provides rendered, simulated 500-Hz annotations.
RVwzfd0hd6.key_idea: Predict the current frame's latent features before fusion, supervised by a frozen teacher that saw the current RGB frame.
RVwzfd0hd6.evidence: HiFE, a dataset built by high-fidelity offline rendering and event simulation with temporally aligned 500-Hz annotations for millisecond-scale detection; the abstract is truncated before results.

YDgH69Voak.one_liner: Conditions noisy-label learning on label source through routing and labeling channels, with a permutation diagnostic choosing the structure.
YDgH69Voak.problem: Noisy-label learning discards which source (website, protocol, annotator) produced each label, although sources' errors need not follow the same pattern and no source is assumed trusted.
YDgH69Voak.method: Label provenance learning observes input, noisy label, and source identity with a latent clean label. Provenance may act through a routing channel (how examples reach sources) and a labeling channel (how sources produce labels), giving four nested structures; provenance-conditioned variational learning (PCVL) fits any of them under one objective, and a permutation diagnostic selects among them before training without clean labels.
YDgH69Voak.key_idea: Treat source identity as an input to routing and labeling channels, and test with a permutation diagnostic which channel the data supports.
YDgH69Voak.evidence: CIFAR-10N, dopanim, and a controlled CIFAR-10 experiment (truncated), compared with DivideMix and provenance-blind PCVL.
YDgH69Voak.claimed_gains: On dopanim, activating only the source-dependent labeling channel improves balanced accuracy over provenance-blind PCVL and DivideMix, while on CIFAR-10N the diagnostic detects no dependency and the provenance-blind structure has the highest mean accuracy; no numbers are stated.

fHJSUhn9Uq.one_liner: Training-free large-small DiT collaboration allocating large-model computation hierarchically across denoising steps, temporal segments, and spatial regions.
fHJSUhn9Uq.problem: DiT video generation is costly because of dense spatiotemporal tokens, and existing large-small collaboration treats the whole video uniformly at each step although the capability gap varies by step, time segment, and region.
fHJSUhn9Uq.method: The small model provides global predictions, while the large model selectively refines difficult regions with preserved spatiotemporal context and smooth prediction fusion, allocating large-model computation progressively at step, temporal, and spatial levels.
fHJSUhn9Uq.key_idea: Use the small model everywhere and invoke the large model only at steps, temporal segments, and spatial regions where the capability gap is large.
fHJSUhn9Uq.evidence: Experiments on Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and CogVideoX measuring speedup and VBench against the corresponding large-only models.
fHJSUhn9Uq.claimed_gains: 2.29-2.93x speedup while keeping VBench within 0.0027 of the corresponding large-only models.

QisYL8dSST.one_liner: Weights stimulus pairs by representational proximity (NW-RSA) and tests linguistic perturbations (CF-RSA) to analyze alignment across LLMs.
QisYL8dSST.problem: Aggregate similarity measures such as standard RSA can obscure how agreement between models varies across geometric scales and which linguistic properties support it.
QisYL8dSST.method: NW-RSA weights stimulus pairs by their proximity in representational space to compare alignment from local neighborhoods to global geometry on a common scale. CF-RSA compares intact representations in one model with representations under controlled linguistic perturbations in another.
QisYL8dSST.key_idea: Weighting stimulus pairs by representational-space proximity yields a scale-resolved RSA, while cross-model comparison against linguistically perturbed inputs identifies which properties support alignment.
QisYL8dSST.evidence: Applied across diverse language models, on broadly sampled natural text and within linguistic equivalence classes that preserve particular aspects of meaning (abstract is truncated).
QisYL8dSST.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports only qualitative findings: strong agreement in coarse geometry, substantial divergence in local neighborhoods).

81bbXpQzvh.one_liner: Compresses frozen video foundation model features into latents with lightweight projectors for diffusion and autoregressive video generation.
81bbXpQzvh.problem: Video generators rely on 3D-VAEs trained for pixel-level reconstruction, whose latent spaces may underrepresent semantic structure.
81bbXpQzvh.method: Lightweight projectors compress multi-scale hierarchical features of a frozen video foundation model into compact 1D sequences or structured 3D grids, giving continuous latents for Diffusion Transformers or discrete tokens (multi-codebook high-dimensional quantization) for autoregressive models. A local-global representation alignment objective in the decoder transfers semantic structure from the frozen encoder and removes the need for KL regularization.
81bbXpQzvh.key_idea: Decode from compressed frozen-foundation-model features, using a local-global representation alignment loss in the decoder instead of KL regularization to retain encoder semantics.
81bbXpQzvh.evidence: Reconstruction in continuous and discrete regimes; class-conditional generation on UCF-101 with autoregressive and diffusion generators; a 4B-scale text-to-video study with randomly initialized diffusion backbones evaluated on VBench against Wan2.1-VAE.
81bbXpQzvh.claimed_gains: On UCF-101, autoregressive and diffusion generators built on VideoRAE reach class-conditional gFVD of 40 and 93 while converging approximately 5x faster than autoencoder baselines, and frozen VideoRAE-3D scores 69.07 versus 68.24 for Wan2.1-VAE on VBench total at 200k steps.

zYUHbTHUw6.one_liner: Decoding-time beam search guided by a log-odds reward from contrastive excellent-versus-poor reasoning contexts, with no parameter updates.
zYUHbTHUw6.problem: Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning needs gradient updates and expert demonstrations, so it cannot be applied at inference time.
zYUHbTHUw6.method: Fixed textual templates that prime the model for excellent versus poor reasoning replace the demonstration, and the log-odds ratio of a candidate answer under the two contexts defines a reward. The optimal KL-regularized policy is a Gibbs reweighting of the base distribution that cannot be decomposed per token, so it is approximated with beam search.
zYUHbTHUw6.key_idea: Use the log-odds of a candidate under counterfactual good-versus-poor reasoning contexts as a reward, and approximate its KL-regularized Gibbs-optimal distribution with beam search.
zYUHbTHUw6.evidence: Experiments on MATH500, HumanEval, and GPQA across multiple model scales (abstract is truncated before the results).

85djEhybB3.one_liner: Parallel speculative drafter using a hybrid Mamba-attention backbone that reuses target KV in place, with no drafter-side KV cache.
85djEhybB3.problem: Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark keep a separate drafter-side KV cache that uses extra GPU memory per request and causes fragmentation in paged serving, while direct target KV reuse alone lowers draft quality at later block positions.
85djEhybB3.method: A hybrid target-context injection initializes Mamba modules with projected last-token target hidden states while attention modules reuse target KVs in place. Mamba's parallel scan preserves block-parallel drafting.
85djEhybB3.key_idea: Inject target context by initializing Mamba modules with the projected last-token target hidden state while attention layers reuse target KV in place, removing the drafter's own KV cache.
85djEhybB3.evidence: Three target models and three workloads, measuring peak throughput across concurrency levels and average KV utilization against the best baseline for each metric.
85djEhybB3.claimed_gains: 5.1-17.3% higher peak throughput across the evaluated concurrency levels and 4.3-24.6% lower average KV utilization than the best baseline for each metric.

0EeNLyAKSb.one_liner: Automated pipeline that builds questions, answers, and verified evidence-page labels from raw documents to train search agents with RL.
0EeNLyAKSb.problem: Correct question-answer pairs do not ensure accurate evidence labels, and incorrect labels can reward irrelevant retrieval or penalize retrieval of supporting evidence.
0EeNLyAKSb.method: A multimodal LLM extracts textual and visual page content, and the distribution of facts across pages guides evidence selection and multi-page question construction. The pipeline checks answer consistency and tests whether each question stays answerable after removing each evidence page in turn; Doc-Search decouples multimodal page perception from a text-based policy and trains it with RL on the answer and retrieval targets.
0EeNLyAKSb.key_idea: Verify evidence labels by removing each evidence page in turn and testing whether the question stays answerable, then use answer and retrieval targets for RL.
0EeNLyAKSb.evidence: DocArena-79K has 79,623 QA pairs from 8,336 documents across 16 domains and 49 languages; experiments cover six multimodal document scenarios and seven text-based QA benchmarks, with pipeline ablations (abstract is truncated).

t5uo6ddUOi.one_liner: Dense spherical local attention on equirectangular grids via distance-corrected longitude positional encoding and row/column-separated linear attention.
t5uo6ddUOi.problem: On equirectangular grids the same physical neighborhood has a latitude-dependent footprint, and prior spherical local operators recover it with location-dependent sampling whose sparse memory access limits GPU utilization.
t5uo6ddUOi.method: DLS combines distance-corrected longitude positional encoding with linear attention that aggregates keys and values separately along rows and columns. This cancels the cross-term involving global longitude, so the global PE encodes local spherical geometry and KV-first aggregation works without constructing local KV fields.
t5uo6ddUOi.key_idea: Separate row and column KV aggregation cancels the global-longitude cross-term, so a distance-corrected global PE encodes local spherical geometry and permits dense KV-first aggregation.
t5uo6ddUOi.evidence: not stated (abstract is truncated before the experiments)

RLI68bLghd.one_liner: Separates relational structure from metric geometry at local and global scales to test representational convergence, using H0 skeleton overlap.
RLI68bLghd.problem: Prior local-global comparisons of representational convergence confound structural scale (local versus global) with what is compared (relational structure versus metric geometry).
RLI68bLghd.method: A controlled 2x2 framework evaluates relational structure and metric geometry at local and global scales, introducing H0 skeleton overlap as a global counterpart to mutual k-nearest neighbors together with matched distance-aware variants. The analysis is extended to a Riemannian metric approximation.
RLI68bLghd.key_idea: Cross scale (local or global) with comparison type (which samples are related versus distances) so convergence is measured separately for relational structure and metric geometry.
RLI68bLghd.evidence: Vision-language models after calibration, plus a Riemannian metric approximation of distance agreement; the abstract is truncated at a further reproduction of the pattern.

TcT89BDdCC.one_liner: Benchmark of 105 multimedia-file terminal tasks plus Terminus-MM, a harness adding native audio and video perception to terminal agents.
TcT89BDdCC.problem: Existing terminal-agent benchmarks focus on text, code, and structured files, though real workflows require working directly with audio and video files.
TcT89BDdCC.method: MMTB has 105 tasks across 5 meta-categories where terminal agents operate directly on audio and video files, with verifiable outputs. Terminus-MM extends Terminus-KIRA with audio and video perception, enabling a same-backbone study of different forms of multimedia access.
TcT89BDdCC.key_idea: Extend an existing terminal-agent harness with native audio and video perception and compare forms of multimedia access on the same backbone to see which evidence agents use.
TcT89BDdCC.evidence: A controlled same-backbone ablation of how native modality access changes task success and evidence gathering; no results are given in the abstract.

tSnNoGfM5d.one_liner: Merges reasoning models by Bayesian optimization with conditional flow matching to preserve feedback discernment under accuracy and token constraints.
tSnNoGfM5d.problem: Some merges of reasoning models improve accuracy and shorten responses but lose feedback discernment, meaning retaining correct answers under misleading advice and correcting wrong answers under valid feedback.
tSnNoGfM5d.method: Merging is cast as constrained optimization that maximizes feedback discernment subject to accuracy and token requirements. A residual flow learns a distribution of coefficient updates across parameter groups from differences between nearby evaluated configurations, Gaussian process surrogates estimate performance and uncertainty, and an acquisition function picks candidates for expensive evaluation.
tSnNoGfM5d.key_idea: Learn a conditional flow over merge-coefficient updates from nearby evaluated configurations and use GP-surrogate Bayesian optimization to pick candidates that maximize discernment under constraints.
tSnNoGfM5d.evidence: Evaluated on eight mathematical tasks or benchmarks (abstract is truncated after 'eight mathematical').

IIXW7J5TQW.one_liner: Plug-and-play module for medical super-resolution that enhances high- and mid-frequency bands separately and fuses them with cross-frequency gating.
IIXW7J5TQW.problem: Medical single-image super-resolution is hindered by the low-frequency bias of deep learning and the distinct semantic roles of mid- and high-frequency components, which uniform enhancement strategies fail to address.
IIXW7J5TQW.method: FARE has a High-Frequency Semantic Amplifier (directional wavelet decomposition with gradient-informed gating) and an Adaptive Mid-Frequency Decoupler (patch-level STFT with a learnable Gaussian band-pass mask), whose outputs are fused by cross-frequency negotiated gating.
IIXW7J5TQW.key_idea: Process high-frequency (wavelet plus gradient gating) and mid-frequency (patch STFT with learnable Gaussian band-pass mask) components in separate branches, then fuse them by cross-frequency gating.
IIXW7J5TQW.evidence: Evaluations on multiple medical image benchmarks (not named) compared with existing methods.
IIXW7J5TQW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent improvements without numbers).

339swmaY5N.one_liner: Verbal critic for coding agents that tracks each correction as a persistent note until the diagnosed problem is resolved.
339swmaY5N.problem: Feedback to long-horizon coding agents can be ineffective or harmful when it misjudges ongoing work or misses the underlying problem, and existing critics rarely track what happens after feedback is delivered.
339swmaY5N.method: Opera triggers reviews periodically and on events, diagnoses issues with typed operators, audits feedback against visible evidence before delivery, and tracks the agent's subsequent actions to separate compliance from actual resolution. Opera-guided rollouts also serve as approximately on-policy training data.
339swmaY5N.key_idea: Treat each correction as a persistent note followed until resolved, with evidence-audited feedback and post-delivery action tracking to separate compliance from resolution.
339swmaY5N.evidence: Test-time critic evaluated on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1 across four policy models against critic baselines; fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on Opera-guided rollouts tested on held-out SWE-Bench Pro repositories.
339swmaY5N.claimed_gains: Improves resolve rate of non-critic agents by up to 12.4, 15.0, and 8.9 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1, and fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on Opera-guided rollouts improves held-out SWE-Bench Pro resolve rate by 10.2 percentage points.

FJcQxyHcM7.one_liner: Studies how tokenizer choice affects factorization error in parallel discrete diffusion decoding, using an exact decomposition by interaction order.
FJcQxyHcM7.problem: Parallel decoding samples positions independently within a denoising step, ignoring dependence between tokens (factorization error), and discrete diffusion models inherit autoregressive tokenizers whose token boundaries determine which dependencies remain.
FJcQxyHcM7.method: Factorization error is decomposed exactly by interaction order, separating schedule-determined weights from tokenizer-determined interactions. BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, and a weighted pointwise mutual information tokenizer are compared (abstract is truncated).
FJcQxyHcM7.key_idea: Decompose factorization error by interaction order into schedule-determined weights and tokenizer-determined interactions, so tokenizers can be ranked by the dependencies they leave across token boundaries.
FJcQxyHcM7.evidence: Theoretical decomposition (lossless tokenizers with equal vocabulary size and encoded lengths reach the same oracle denoising loss but can differ in factorization error) and a comparison of BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, and a weighted PMI tokenizer; results are truncated.

WuldvnhGHs.one_liner: Makes quantization itself the unlearning operator by steering code assignment with forget and retain activation statistics.
WuldvnhGHs.problem: Low-bit quantization can undo unlearning by discarding the parameter changes it introduced, and existing methods still treat unlearning and quantization as two separate steps.
WuldvnhGHs.method: Quantization maps continuous weights to discrete codes while retaining behavior on retain data and inducing forgetting on forget data, directly building an unlearned low-bit model without a preceding continuous-space update. Activation statistics from forget and retain calibration data give an element-wise score that sets where and how strongly a code deviates from the reconstruction-driven code, and ordinary quantization error and code-displacement error are compensated separately.
WuldvnhGHs.key_idea: Score each weight element from forget/retain activation statistics to decide how far its quantization code deviates from the reconstruction-driven code, compensating quantization error and displacement error separately.
WuldvnhGHs.evidence: not stated (abstract is truncated before the experiments)

XLQEZJpeZN.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,768 queries testing embodied agents' memory recall and progress tracking across navigation and manipulation, with an R&R Agent.
XLQEZJpeZN.problem: Embodied agents must recall past experience and track progress while acting, and these memory requirements need systematic evaluation across navigation and manipulation.
XLQEZJpeZN.method: R&R-Bench has 300 contexts across 228 simulated houses (43 hours of experience), four task families (Finding, Restore, Resume, Routine), and three evaluation conditions (memory QA, execution given correct goals, full pipeline). R&R Agent combines textual records, tagged visual evidence, and request-conditioned retrieval.
XLQEZJpeZN.key_idea: Vary request scope, evidence source, and target concealment across four memory-demanding task families, and evaluate memory QA separately from execution to relate recall to task success.
XLQEZJpeZN.evidence: Evaluated systems on 300 contexts and 1,768 queries; visual memory better supports spatial recall and passively observed information, while textual memory better supports unfinished-work recovery, storage-rule inference, and progress tracking; separate placement experiments test retrieved visual goals for manipulation.
XLQEZJpeZN.claimed_gains: No numbers are stated; R&R Agent is reported to achieve the highest task-average memory-QA accuracy and full-pipeline success across all four families among evaluated methods that construct memory from experience.

BWIuBZ3JpX.one_liner: Learned augmentation for wearable contrastive learning: a gate keeps target-modal components and cross-attention from helper sensors synthesizes the rest.
BWIuBZ3JpX.problem: Augmented views for multimodal wearable contrastive learning need enough variation while preserving intra-modal semantics and cross-modal relationships, but faithful cross-modal reconstruction gives little variation and generation from other sensors alone can discard target-specific information.
BWIuBZ3JpX.method: ReWeave uses a learned gate to preserve selected components in a frozen, variance-covariance-regularized latent space while temporal cross-attention synthesizes the residual from helper signals. A sparsity penalty limits direct target retention, matched attention is compared with a control using helper keys from another instance, and decoding the edited embeddings yields signal-space augmentations.
BWIuBZ3JpX.key_idea: Learn which target-modality information to retain via a gate in latent space and replace the rest using cross-attention over synchronized companion modalities, regularized by a sparsity penalty.
BWIuBZ3JpX.evidence: Pretraining on 3,565 hours of wearable recordings, with frozen representations evaluated on four disjoint evaluation sets (abstract is truncated after 'four disjoint').

rEjoDUqCy2.one_liner: Benchmark that varies high-level driving intentions on fixed scenes to evaluate in-context decision-making of end-to-end driving models.
rEjoDUqCy2.problem: Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks assess trajectory quality (safety, compliance, comfort, progress) but leave context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized.
rEjoDUqCy2.method: PlanContext builds paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, defines six driving contexts, and counts contextual success only when decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety all hold.
rEjoDUqCy2.key_idea: Pair evaluations that change only the high-level intention on an identical scene, and score success jointly on decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety.
rEjoDUqCy2.evidence: 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models, with analysis by decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction.
rEjoDUqCy2.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context decision-making).

Q2kdLm7ObB.one_liner: Activation steering that composes per-category safety directions by estimated risk and rotates hidden states with norm preserved.
Q2kdLm7ObB.problem: A single prompt can involve several harm categories, steering toward safety in one category can leave another unaddressed, and existing adaptive steering does not coordinate direction and strength when categories co-occur.
Q2kdLm7ObB.method: CAM-Steer estimates per-category risk by comparing the current hidden state with safe and unsafe prototypes, uses the risks to combine category safety directions into one steering direction and to set intervention strength, then rotates the hidden state along that direction by a risk-determined angle while preserving its norm.
Q2kdLm7ObB.key_idea: Estimate per-category risk by comparing hidden states with safe/unsafe prototypes, weight category safety directions by it, and rotate the hidden state by a risk-determined angle preserving its norm.
Q2kdLm7ObB.evidence: Experiments across three LLM backbones and seven harm categories, measuring average defense success rate against evaluated baselines (abstract is truncated).
Q2kdLm7ObB.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that CAM-Steer outperforms the evaluated baselines in average defense success rate).

eq7y6c6jg7.one_liner: Context compression with nested Matryoshka tokens and a tolerance-conditioned allocator that sets per-chunk token counts by information content.
eq7y6c6jg7.problem: Most context compression methods fix one compression ratio at training time, so every context of a given length gets the same allocation regardless of its information content.
eq7y6c6jg7.method: MANTA encodes each chunk as Matryoshka tokens (nested, with valid arbitrary-length prefixes) and uses a lightweight Elastic Allocator, conditioned on a tolerance, to decide how many tokens each chunk keeps from the excess loss its content would incur. The target is the minimal sufficient allocation whose excess loss against the full allocation stays below a global tolerance.
eq7y6c6jg7.key_idea: Nested prefix-valid Matryoshka tokens let an allocator conditioned on a loss tolerance choose per-chunk token counts at inference time, targeting the minimal allocation whose excess loss stays within tolerance.
eq7y6c6jg7.evidence: Compared with existing context compression methods across different compression ratios, in domain and out of domain (abstract is truncated).
eq7y6c6jg7.claimed_gains: Improves average token-F1 by 9.3% relative in domain and 5.4% out of domain (the abstract text is truncated after 'out of') over existing compression methods.

cNwvzev1GV.one_liner: Streaming causal autoregressive diffusion video-to-audio model producing spatial stereo sound with chunk-wise prompt control for interactive world models.
cNwvzev1GV.problem: Generated world-model environments are silent, and adding sound requires real-time generation, interactive control during the stream, and stereo audio aligned to scene geometry and camera motion.
cNwvzev1GV.method: A streaming causal autoregressive diffusion architecture synthesizes audio chunks, an audio-centric captioning pipeline with chunk-indexed prompt scheduling allows mid-stream manipulation of sound events, and stereo supervision is curated from diverse stereo and ambisonic data.
cNwvzev1GV.key_idea: Generate audio chunk by chunk with causal autoregressive diffusion, schedule per-chunk text prompts for control, and train on curated stereo and ambisonic data for spatial alignment.
cNwvzev1GV.evidence: Extensive experiments reported on open-domain video-to-audio benchmarks, compared with bidirectional models on acoustic quality and spatial alignment.
cNwvzev1GV.claimed_gains: Real-time factor of 0.41, and matching or outperforming bidirectional models in both acoustic quality and spatial alignment (no other numbers stated).

Y1ejE9H8Ee.one_liner: Alpha-formula discovery agent with event-driven Reward-Jump Memory and an action-conditioned neural SDE critic over discounted returns.
Y1ejE9H8Ee.problem: In formulaic alpha discovery, feedback arrives mainly when a complete expression is evaluated, so the alpha pool does not preserve the history of realized feedback and the value of intermediate construction actions is uncertain.
Y1ejE9H8Ee.method: Reward-Jump Memory is a latent state that stays fixed during token construction and updates only at terminal evaluation events using the realized pool reward and outcome. An action-conditioned SDE return critic represents future discounted returns with stochastic particles trained with a distributional Bellman objective (energy-distance matching, mean calibration, jump regularization), and the particles guide action selection through their mean and uncertainty.
Y1ejE9H8Ee.key_idea: Update a persistent latent memory only at terminal evaluation events and model future returns as stochastic SDE particles trained with a distributional Bellman loss.
Y1ejE9H8Ee.evidence: Multiple equity universes, forecasting horizons, and random seeds, with ablations of persistent evaluation history, stochastic return modeling, and distributional supervision.

ittJU5NZcd.one_liner: Training-free edit of the answer-token rows in an MLLM's vocabulary projection using a forensic direction from real and fake images.
ittJU5NZcd.problem: Fine-tuning MLLMs with binary real/fake supervision for AI-generated image detection overfits to training fake patterns and fails to generalize, while frozen MLLM representations already hold forensic information the verbalizer does not fully use.
ittJU5NZcd.method: FRA estimates a forensic direction with a boundary offset from real images and a single generator's fake images and encodes it into the vocabulary-projection weights of the real/fake answer tokens, with no backbone update or gradient-based training. It preserves the original distance and midpoint between the two answer rows.
ittJU5NZcd.key_idea: Write a forensic direction and boundary offset into the real/fake answer-token rows of the vocabulary projection while preserving their distance and midpoint, so the boundary stays calibrated.
ittJU5NZcd.evidence: Cross-generator detection using the same training data as the evaluated methods, compared with LoRA-based adaptations, across training generators, training-set sizes, and MLLM backbones.
ittJU5NZcd.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports the best overall cross-generator detection performance, outperforming LoRA-based adaptations, without numbers).

hoVTOkIhvt.one_liner: Streaming video MLLM memory that internalizes query-relevant evidence into compact latent tokens via hierarchical memory and test-time optimization.
hoVTOkIhvt.problem: Store-and-retrieve memory banks keep historical evidence as external visual context, preventing it from being internalized into a compact, evolving latent memory that guides streaming reasoning.
hoVTOkIhvt.method: LatentStream has a Query-Agnostic Hierarchical Streaming Memory that organizes visual history into short-, mid-, and long-term levels via Jenks-guided adaptive consolidation, and a Hierarchical Latent Memory Evolution in which groups of latent memory tokens with progressively expanding receptive fields iteratively retrieve historical evidence and internalize it. A third component is cut off in the abstract.
hoVTOkIhvt.key_idea: Shift streaming memory from store-and-retrieve to retrieve-and-internalize: latent tokens with expanding memory receptive fields pull evidence from a Jenks-consolidated hierarchy into compact latent memory.
hoVTOkIhvt.evidence: not stated (abstract is truncated before the experiments)

j4CCWal5Zf.one_liner: Instruction data selection using Matryoshka sparse autoencoder concepts organized in a hierarchy with quality-weighted diminishing-return coverage.
j4CCWal5Zf.problem: Instruction-tuning corpora are semantically redundant, and existing diversity-aware selectors rely on generated semantic tags and explicit graph structures that add annotation and preprocessing overhead.
